# RandomGenerator

A source of uniformly distributed 64-bit words.

```rux
pub interface RandomGenerator {
    func NextUint64(self: &var Self) -> uint64;
}
```

The single operation every generator supplies. Implementations must advance their own state, so the receiver
is a mutable reference. Borrowed interface views and generic bounds both keep it the caller's state that
advances.

## Requirements

<h3 id="next-uint64"><code>NextUint64</code></h3>

```rux
func NextUint64(self: &var Self) -> uint64
```

The next 64-bit word, and the state advanced past it.

**Returns**: the next 64 bits

<h3 id="fill-bytes"><code>FillBytes&lt;G&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FillBytes<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, into: var char8[..])
```

Fills `into` with random bytes.
The words are consumed least significant byte first, and a partial final word contributes its low bytes and
discards the rest — so the same `into.length` always consumes the same number of words, and two runs that
fill buffers of the same size stay in step.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Extract.rux#L15)

<h3 id="next-uint32"><code>NextUint32&lt;G&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NextUint32<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G) -> uint32
```

The next 32-bit word: the low half of a 64-bit one.
A whole word is consumed and half of it discarded, which costs nothing and keeps the word stream aligned --
a generator that handed out the halves in turn would produce different sequences depending on how many
narrow draws happened to precede a wide one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Extract.rux#L37)

<h3 id="next-float64"><code>NextFloat64&lt;G&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NextFloat64<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G) -> float64
```

A `float64` uniformly distributed in `[0, 1)`.
Built from the top 53 bits of a word, which is exactly the number a `float64` can hold without rounding: every
value produced is a multiple of 2^-53, each equally likely, and none is ever exactly one. Dividing a whole
word by 2^64 instead would round — and rounding upward at the top would produce exactly one, which callers
scaling into an array index do not expect.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Extract.rux#L79)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type     | Description              |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from |

**Returns**: a value in `[0, 1)`, with 53 bits of significance
